plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 after material_data failures in two prior iterations. The core issue appears to be material identifier resolution in the downstream registry. Three complementary routes proposed: (1) 20-layer Ge/ZnS 2-cavity Fabry-Perot with analytically-derived quarter-wave initialization at 4.45 μm, (2) 24-layer Ge/ZnS 3-cavity design for enhanced stopband blocking, (3) 20-layer Si/ZnS alternative material pair in case Ge has registry availability issues. All routes use explicit finite layer counts, bounded thickness variables [80-600 nm], and pre-validation of material optical constants before optimization. Evidence supports Ge/ZnS for 3-5 μm mid-IR with high index contrast and low absorption.

routes.title: 20-Layer Ge/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot with Quarter-Wave Seeding
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A two-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge (high-index) and ZnS (low-index) dielectric materials, initialized with quarter-wave thicknesses at 4.45 μm center wavelength, will achieve dual-band transmission at 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm with stopband suppression at 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm when thicknesses are computationally optimized within [80, 600] nm bounds.
routes.design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter design: alternating quarter-wave layers of high and low index transparent materials form Bragg reflectors around cavity spacer layers. Computational optimization adjusts layer thicknesses from quarter-wave seeds to shape passband profile and enhance out-of-band blocking.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_4 | Ge (cavity1) | [ZnS/Ge]_2 | ZnS (cavity2) | [Ge/ZnS]_4 | CaF2 substrate. Total 20 finite layers: 8 mirror pairs + 2 cavity layers + coupling stack.
design_variables: Initial values set to t = λ₀/(4n) at λ₀ = 4450 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds [80, 600] nm for deposition feasibility
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: t_layer = λ₀/(4n_material) for Bragg reflector center wavelength
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: (φ₁ + φ₂ - 2δ)/2 = kπ for maximum transmittance
Multi-cavity coupling produces square-shaped passband profiles
expected_advantages: Ge/ZnS has high index contrast (~4.0 vs ~2.3) in mid-IR for strong reflectivity
20 layers balances performance with fabrication complexity
Quarter-wave seeding provides physically meaningful initialization
Two cavities enable dual-band or broadened single-band response
known_risks: Material registry may not have Ge or ZnS optical constants in 4-5 μm range
Quarter-wave initialization may not align with dual-band requirement
Thickness tolerance sensitivity increases with layer count
Absorption in Ge may reduce peak transmittance if not properly accounted
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 20-layer dielectric multilayer bandpass filter on CaF2 substrate under air incidence at normal angle. Use Germanium (Ge) as high-index material and Zinc Sulfide (ZnS) as low-index material. Stack topology: Air | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge (cavity1) | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS (cavity2) | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | Ge | ZnS | CaF2. Initialize all layer thicknesses using quarter-wave formula t = 4450 nm / (4 × n_material) where n_Ge ≈ 4.0 and n_ZnS ≈ 2.3 at 4.45 μm, giving initial Ge thickness ~278 nm and ZnS thickness ~484 nm. Set optimization bounds for all thicknesses to [80 nm, 600 nm]. Optimize the 20 thickness variables to maximize mean transmittance in passbands [4150-4350 nm] and [4550-4750 nm] while minimizing mean transmittance in stopbands [3600-4000 nm] and [4850-5200 nm]. Use coherent transfer-matrix method with frequency-domain plane-wave illumination. Validate material refractive indices exist in registry for 3.6-5.2 μm wavelength range before optimization. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm array. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
routes.revision_reason: Prior route_03 iterations failed on material_data. This revision: (1) uses explicit quarter-wave thickness initialization from analytical formula instead of random bounds, (2) specifies exact 20-layer topology with cavity positions, (3) adds mandatory pre-validation of material optical constants in registry, (4) tightens thickness bounds to [80, 600] nm based on deposition feasibility evidence.

routes.title: 24-Layer Ge/ZnS Three-Cavity Fabry-Perot for Enhanced Stopband Blocking
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A three-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter using Ge/ZnS with 24 total layers will achieve stronger stopband suppression (lower transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm) compared to two-cavity designs, while maintaining high passband transmittance, due to increased mirror pair count and additional cavity coupling.
routes.design_principle: Three-cavity Fabry-Perot design with increased layer count provides more degrees of freedom for shaping passband profile and deepening stopband rejection. Evidence shows 24-layer filters achieved OD3 blocking with ~100% peak transmittance in mid-IR.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Ge/ZnS]_5 | Ge (cavity1) | [ZnS/Ge]_2 | ZnS (cavity2) | [Ge/ZnS]_2 | Ge (cavity3) | [ZnS/Ge]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 24 finite layers.
design_variables: Initial values set to t = λ₀/(4n) at λ₀ = 4450 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Total film thickness ~8-10 μm based on evidence
theory_basis: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot theory: additional cavities flatten passband top and steepen band edges
Layer count vs bandwidth tradeoff: more layers enable narrower bandwidth but increase fabrication sensitivity
OD3 blocking (transmittance < 10⁻³) achievable with 24-layer mid-IR filters
expected_advantages: 24 layers at maximum allowed count provides most design freedom
Three cavities enable better dual-band shaping than two cavities
Evidence shows 24-layer Ge/ZnS achieved OD3 blocking in 3-5 μm range
Higher layer count improves stopband suppression depth
known_risks: Total thickness ~8-10 μm may cause stress/adhesion issues
More variables increase optimization complexity and convergence time
Same material registry risk as route_03_refine_01

routes.title: 20-Layer Si/ZnS Two-Cavity Fabry-Perot Alternative Material Pair
routes.scientific_hypothesis: If Ge/ZnS fails due to material registry unavailability, Silicon (Si) with Zinc Sulfide (ZnS) provides an alternative high-contrast dielectric pair for mid-IR bandpass filters. Si has refractive index ~3.4 at 4-5 μm (lower than Ge's ~4.0 but still sufficient contrast with ZnS ~2.3), and Si is more commonly available in thin-film optical constant databases.
routes.design_principle: Same multi-cavity Fabry-Perot design principle as Ge/ZnS routes, but substituting Si for Ge as high-index material. Lower index contrast (3.4 vs 2.3 instead of 4.0 vs 2.3) requires slightly more layers or thicker mirrors for equivalent reflectivity, but Si has lower absorption in some mid-IR ranges.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [Si/ZnS]_5 | Si (cavity1) | [ZnS/Si]_2 | ZnS (cavity2) | [Si/ZnS]_5 | CaF2 substrate. Total 20 finite layers (increased mirror pairs to compensate for lower index contrast).
design_variables: Initial values set to t = λ₀/(4n) at λ₀ = 4450 nm with n_Si ≈ 3.4
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm band
Maximize mean transmittance in 4.55-4.75 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 4.85-5.20 μm band
manufacturing_considerations: Si and ZnS are conventional depositable IR dielectrics
theory_basis: High-low index material pair selection principle: significant refractive index difference improves reflectivity per layer pair
Si/ZnS is a documented alternative to Ge/ZnS for mid-IR filters
Lower index contrast requires more layer pairs for equivalent stopband depth
expected_advantages: Si optical constants more commonly available in thin-film databases than Ge
Si has lower absorption coefficient than Ge in some mid-IR ranges
Same design topology as route_03_refine_01 enables direct material-pair comparison
Fallback option if Ge/ZnS routes fail on material_data
known_risks: Lower index contrast (3.4 vs 2.3) reduces reflectivity per layer pair
May require more than 20 layers to match Ge/ZnS stopband performance
Si absorption characteristics must be verified for 3.6-5.2 μm range
Still subject to material registry availability
